question: Why does == often give unexpected results when comparing two Java String objects for equality?
options: Strings cannot be compared at all
== compares object references, not the string's content, so use .equals() to compare content
Strings must be converted to char arrays first
explanation: == on objects compares whether two references point to the same object in memory; two separately created Strings with equal content may still be different objects, so .equals() should be used to compare their content.
